title: Effect of intercropping on crop yield compared to sole cropping
research_question: Does intercropping (growing two or more crops simultaneously in the same field) increase crop yield compared to sole cropping / monoculture?
population_description: Field crops (cereals, legumes, vegetables) grown in intercropping systems
intervention_description: Intercropping (strip, row, relay, mixed) with any companion crop
comparator_description: Sole cropping / monoculture of the same crop
outcome_description: Crop yield (grain yield, biomass, total yield) of the primary crop or combined system
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is yield UNDER INTERCROPPING, Control is yield UNDER SOLE CROPPING
Some papers report yields of BOTH crops in the intercrop - extract each separately vs its own sole crop control
Do NOT confuse intercropping with crop rotation - intercropping is SIMULTANEOUS growing
Relay intercropping has temporal overlap but crops are not identical in timing - still counts as intercropping
LER > 1 means intercropping is MORE productive per unit land than monocultures
Some papers report 'partial LER' for each crop - extract both partial and total LER if available
Additive vs replacement designs differ - in additive, intercrop density is higher than sole crop
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of EACH crop species separately in the intercrop AND the corresponding sole crop control
2. Treatment = crop yield UNDER intercropping; Control = same crop yield under sole cropping/monoculture
3. If LER is reported, extract it as a separate outcome row
6. Record both the primary and companion crop species
7. Record intercropping arrangement type (strip, row, relay, mixed)
benchmark_source: Yu et al. 2015 (Agronomy for Sustainable Development 35:767-778)
benchmark_notes: LER = 1.22 across 100 studies; 22% more total land needed for monocultures to match intercrop output. Also supported by Li et al. 2020 finding similar magnitudes.
